short: Binding SnO2 Nanocrystals in Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Sheets
title: Binding SnO2 Nanocrystals in Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Sheets as Anode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: SnO2 anodes offer high Li capacity but suffer huge volume change, Sn aggregation and unstable SEI, so cycling fades. Binding SnO2 nanocrystals inside N-doped graphene sheets should give fast e-/Li+ transport, buffer volume change and stop Sn aggregation.
states.detail: Absorbed: b1 (HYP/need), b2 (HYP/hypothesis), b3 (DES/base_system), b4 (DES/modification), b5 (DES/route), b6 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: SnO2 nanocrystals are chemically bonded to N-RGO through interfacial Sn-N-C and Sn-O-C bonds. Uniform SnO2 nanocrystals are homogeneously distributed throughout the graphene sheets.
states.detail: Absorbed: b7 (STR/interface), b8 (STR/microstructure/distribution), b9 (STR/microstructure/porosity). Premises: Higher C K-edge intensity at ~285/288 eV marks carbon bonded to N and O species [43]

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Electrons reach the NCs through the conducting graphene, Li+ through micropores; graphene buffers volume change and limits SEI; bonds stop Sn aggregation. High reversible Li storage capacity, ~1100-1200 mA h g-1 in the first cycles

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Good rate capability: ~1074 to ~417 mA h g-1 from 0.5 to 20 A g-1, recovering ~1034 at 0.5 A g-1. Long cycling: ~1346 mA h g-1 after 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiency near 100%

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Binding SnO2 nanocrystals in N-doped graphene gives a high-capacity, high-rate, long-life Li-ion anode
